readingEdge.paragraph: In the summer of 1954, Boeing tested a new jet prototype called the 367-80. Nicknamed the Dash 80, it featured swept wings and four jet engines. Its first flight took place on July 15, 1954. Engineers used the aircraft to explore the possibilities of fast commercial flight and aerial refueling. The experiment helped lead to the Boeing 707 passenger airliner and the KC-135 tanker. Today, the original Dash 80 belongs to the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, where visitors can see an important chapter in aviation history.
